findings.description: CON-SUP-103 permits a task to start at the limit and defines a late start as later than the limit. Detecting a fault at expiry when the task has not started can also fault a start exactly at the limit.
findings.requested_change: Define detection and boundary handling so a start at the configured limit is accepted and a later start is detected, consistent with the specified measurement resolution.

findings.description: The trigger requires execution longer than the limit, but the response is required at the limit's expiry. The statement does not resolve whether completion exactly at the limit is accepted, as CON-SUP-103 requires.
findings.requested_change: Specify how the expiry detection distinguishes completion at the limit from execution beyond it, including the 100 µs measurement resolution.

findings.description: The trigger refers to an allowed range without identifying its contents or referencing CON-SUP-115, which identifies a limit longer than the task period, a zero period and an unknown task as configuration faults.
findings.requested_change: State or precisely reference the configuration conditions that trigger fault code 9.

findings.description: The unconditional refresh at the end of each cycle conflicts with SYS-SUP-013, which withholds every watchdog service action while a fault is detected. STK-SUP-005 permits servicing only while every supervised task is healthy.
findings.requested_change: Qualify the refresh obligation with the permitted health conditions and reconcile it with the fault reaction.

findings.description: The condition 'while a fault is detected' does not establish when withholding starts or ends, including whether it persists after detection until reset. STK-SUP-005 requires watchdogs to be serviced only while every supervised task is healthy.
findings.requested_change: Define the fault and health conditions that govern withholding and the event that ends it.

findings.description: The requirement detects a mismatch with a stored reference, but OP-SYS-004 leaves the reference and comparison method undefined. A verifier cannot determine which program changes must cause a mismatch or establish the expected result from the stated condition.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-004 as blocking.

findings.description: The unconditional instruction to drive status high when integrity checks pass can conflict with the safe-state latch in SYS-SUP-009 and SYS-SUP-028, which must remain in the safe state until power-on reset. CON-SUP-109 defines low as not operational.
findings.requested_change: Define the conditions for indicating operational status so that passing integrity checks cannot override a latched safe state.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 requires transmission after entry into the safe state, whereas this requirement only sets a 10 ms deadline from detection and permits transmission before safe-state entry. SYS-SUP-022 allows up to 50 ms for entry.
findings.requested_change: Reconcile the required transmission order with both deadlines, recording a blocking decision if the input timing and ordering cannot be satisfied together.

findings.description: OP-SYS-006 leaves the origin and wrap behavior of 'ms since start' undecided. A verifier cannot determine the expected timestamp across resets or counter wrap.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-006 as blocking.

findings.description: The unconditional reset request after safe-state entry conflicts with SYS-SUP-009, which latches the safe state for an out-of-range configuration until power-on reset, and can conflict with SYS-SUP-028's repeated-fault latch.
findings.requested_change: Specify when the reset request is suppressed for a latched safe state, consistent with the product decisions.

findings.description: The required code 8 fault report has an entity field under SYS-SUP-024, but CON-SUP-112 does not define its value for a watchdog reset. OP-SYS-003 records the missing decision.
findings.requested_change: Define the report entity for fault code 8 after the product decision is made.

findings.description: OP-SYS-005 leaves the status state values and the meaning of fault count undefined. A verifier cannot determine the expected STS response for a given operating and reset history.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-005 as blocking.

findings.description: The trigger is a measured delay between release and start. If the task never starts, that delay has no completed start event, so the statement does not clearly require late-start detection while the task is still waiting. CON-SUP-103 defines a late start relative to the configured limit.
findings.requested_change: Clarify whether and when a late-start fault is detected if the task has not started after its limit expires, resolving the behavior with the product owner if necessary.

findings.description: CON-SUP-103 says an overrun is detected when the execution limit expires. The requirement permits detection only when measured execution time is greater than the limit, and its rationale explicitly delays detection until the first measurement step after expiry.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the expiry-time detection rule and equality boundary with the product owner, record any needed open point, and align the requirement with that decision.

findings.description: The statement requires both detection of configuration fault code 9 and latching the safe state. Detection can succeed while the latch fails, so the two behaviors are independently judgeable.
findings.requested_change: Separate configuration-fault detection and safe-state latching into independently verifiable obligations.

findings.description: This item requires a window-watchdog refresh at the end of every cycle in which no fault is detected. SYS-SUP-013 prohibits every watchdog service action while the safe state is latched and after a fault is detected until reset, including cycles with no new detection.
findings.requested_change: Make the refresh condition explicitly consistent with the persistent fault and latched-state withholding obligations in SYS-SUP-013.

findings.description: The requirement calls for detection at the moment elapsed time exceeds the limit, while its rationale calls for detection at the first 100 µs measurement step after the limit. CON-SUP-103 specifies 100 µs resolution but does not define how elapsed time or the detection instant is quantized. A verifier cannot determine the required detection time for a limit crossing between measurement steps.
findings.requested_change: Define a source-supported, measurable detection instant and the treatment of limit crossings between measurement steps; record a blocking open point if a product decision is needed.

findings.description: The requirement demands detection at the expiry instant while accepting a completion at that same instant. OP-SYS-009 acknowledges that the treatment of a completion in the same 100 µs measurement step as expiry is unspecified. A verifier cannot decide whether such a completion must cause fault code 3.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-009 as blocking and obtain the decision needed to define the expiry-boundary behavior.

findings.description: The requirement mandates detection at the exact expiry instant. CON-SUP-105 identifies expiry as the instant from which the 50 ms safe-state reaction is measured; it does not require late-start detection at that instant. CON-SUP-103 explicitly specifies expiry detection for an overrun, but does not state that deadline for a late start.
findings.requested_change: Establish a source-supported late-start detection deadline, or record the missing decision as a blocking open point.

findings.description: The requirement accepts a start exactly at expiry but requires detection at expiry if the task has not started. CON-SUP-103 specifies 100 µs measurement resolution, and OP-SYS-009 leaves unresolved how a start in the same measurement step as expiry is distinguished. Tests away from the boundary do not establish pass or fail at that boundary.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-009 as blocking so the boundary behaviour can be decided before the requirement is verified.

findings.description: The requirement detects a mismatch with a stored reference, but OP-SYS-004 leaves the reference and comparison method undefined. A verifier cannot determine which program changes must cause a mismatch.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-004 as blocking and obtain the decision needed to specify a verifiable integrity check.

findings.description: OP-SYS-006 leaves the origin and wrap behavior of the fault-report timestamp undefined, so the expected value across resets and counter wrap cannot be determined.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-006 as blocking and specify the timestamp origin and wrap behavior.

findings.description: The required code 8 fault report includes an entity field under SYS-SUP-024, but CON-SUP-112 does not define its value for a watchdog reset.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-003 and specify the entity value for a watchdog-reset report.

findings.description: OP-SYS-005 leaves the status state values and the meaning of fault count undefined. The expected STS response cannot be determined for a given operating and reset history.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-005 as blocking and specify the state values and fault-count semantics.

findings.description: The requirement demands detection at expiry while accepting a completion at that instant. OP-SYS-009 leaves the treatment of a completion in the same 100 µs measurement step as expiry unspecified, preventing a boundary verdict.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-009 as blocking and resolve the completion-at-expiry measurement and detection behavior.

findings.description: The requirement mandates late-start detection at the exact expiry instant. CON-SUP-105 identifies expiry as the reference for the safe-state reaction, but does not require late-start detection at that instant; CON-SUP-103 expressly specifies expiry detection for an overrun.
findings.requested_change: Align the late-start detection deadline with the cited sources, or obtain a product decision supporting the required deadline.

findings.description: The requirement accepts a start exactly at expiry but requires detection at expiry if the task has not started. OP-SYS-009 leaves unresolved how a start in the same 100 µs measurement step as expiry is distinguished.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-009 as blocking and resolve the start-at-expiry measurement and detection behavior.

findings.description: STK-SUP-005 requires the hardware watchdogs to be serviced while supervised tasks are healthy. SYS-SUP-011 requires window-watchdog refresh, and SYS-SUP-010 requires an independent-watchdog reset after 100 ms without service, but the set never requires independent-watchdog service during healthy operation.
findings.requested_change: Specify the independent-watchdog servicing obligation and its relationship to healthy operation, using a product decision if its timing cannot be derived from the inputs.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the classified reset cause to be readable by the service tool. SYS-SUP-031 only sends it in a start-up message, while SYS-SUP-033 through SYS-SUP-035 provide no request that returns it. OP-SYS-002 records the missing interface decision.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-002 and specify how the service tool reads the classified reset cause.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 requires the fault report to be transmitted after safe-state entry. SYS-SUP-023 specifies only a 10 ms deadline from detection, and SYS-SUP-027 requires the report before reset; neither requires transmission after entry. OP-SYS-008 records the unresolved ordering and timing decision.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-008 and specify the required relationship between safe-state entry and report transmission.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 states that both the safe-state latch and fault history are kept in memory that does not survive power loss. SYS-SUP-029 requires survival across software and watchdog resets but does not address loss of fault history on power loss.
findings.requested_change: Specify the required fault-history behavior on power loss in accordance with CON-SUP-110.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-024 requires an entity in every fault report, but SYS-SUP-026 defines entities only for codes 1 through 7. CON-SUP-112 also defines codes 8 and 9; OP-SYS-003 records their missing entity values.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-003 and specify the report entity for configuration-out-of-range faults as well as watchdog-reset faults.

findings.description: The requirement detects a mismatch with a stored reference, but OP-SYS-004 leaves the reference and comparison method undefined. A verifier cannot determine which program changes must cause a mismatch.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-004 as blocking.

findings.description: OP-SYS-006 leaves the origin and wrap behavior of the fault-report timestamp undefined, so the expected value across resets and counter wrap cannot be determined.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-006 as blocking.

findings.description: The required code 8 fault report includes an entity field under SYS-SUP-024, but CON-SUP-112 does not define its value for a watchdog reset.
findings.requested_change: Define the entity value for a watchdog-reset fault report after the product decision is made.

findings.description: OP-SYS-005 leaves the status state values and the meaning of fault count undefined. The expected STS response cannot be determined for a given operating and reset history.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-005 as blocking.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-024 requires an entity in every fault report, but SYS-SUP-026 defines entities only for codes 1 through 7. CON-SUP-112 also defines codes 8 and 9; OP-SYS-003 records their missing entity values.
findings.requested_change: Define the entity values for fault codes 8 and 9 after the product decision is made.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-003 detects a late-start fault only when the task starts, while CON-SUP-105 measures the reaction from expiry of a timing limit. OP-SYS-010 defers the detection instant for a task that never starts, leaving the timely response to that condition unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-010 as blocking.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-013 withholds watchdog service during a latched safe state, while SYS-SUP-010 and SYS-SUP-012 require watchdog resets after missed service. The set does not establish that outputs remain in the safe state through those resets, although CON-SUP-110 requires the latched safe state until power-on reset.
findings.requested_change: Specify and assess the interaction of watchdog resets with the latched safe state, including output behavior throughout each reset.

findings.description: The independent-watchdog service obligation constrains only intervals between consecutive services. It does not bound the first service after reset or require any service at all, so it permits the 100 ms timeout in SYS-SUP-010 during otherwise healthy operation.
findings.requested_change: Specify the first service and continuing service obligations needed to prevent independent-watchdog timeout during healthy operation.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-021 drives the status signal high whenever no fault is currently detected and the latch is clear. After a transient fault clears but before reset, this can conflict with the safe-state recovery sequence in STK-SUP-010 and CON-SUP-110, while SYS-SUP-013 continues to treat the fault as active until reset.
findings.requested_change: Define the status signal behavior from fault detection through reset consistently with the safe-state recovery sequence.

findings.description: The program-code check relies on a stored reference, but OP-SYS-004 leaves the reference and comparison method undefined. The set does not establish which changes to the application image must be detected.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-004 as blocking and obtain the integrity-check acceptance criteria needed to verify the requirement.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 requires milliseconds since start, but OP-SYS-006 leaves the timestamp origin and wrap behavior undefined. Expected report values across resets and counter wrap cannot be determined.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-006 as blocking and obtain the timestamp origin and wrap behavior.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-024 requires an entity in every fault report, but CON-SUP-112 does not define the entity for the code 8 watchdog-reset report.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the entity value for a watchdog-reset report.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-022 requires the outputs and status signal to be driven low within 50 ms, but does not require them to remain low until reset for an unlatched fault. SYS-SUP-046 provides that hold only while the safe state is latched, leaving the recovery sequence in STK-SUP-010 and CON-SUP-110 incomplete.
findings.requested_change: Specify how the safe-state outputs and status are maintained from entry until the recovery reset for an unlatched fault.
